title: NGDB-Zoo: Towards Efficient and Scalable Neural Graph Databases Training
claim: Complex multi-hop queries can be answered by compiling them into operator plans executed directly in embedding space, avoiding graph traversal.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right with query stacked above plan, dashed arrows in embedding space
description: Three rounded, pastel-colored panels illustrate the task. Top-left, an orange panel (A) 'Logical Query' holds a natural-language question: 'Where did Indy Car Champions who won a race in Phoenix graduate?'. Below it, a blue panel (B) 'Query Computation Plan' shows a small graph. Entities 'Indy Car Champion' and 'Phoenix' (blue nodes) pass through relation nodes 'Instance of' and 'Won at' (green). Both feed an 'Intersection' node (orange), which leads to a 'graduatesFrom' node. On the right, a larger yellow panel (C) 'Operations in the embedding space' redraws the plan as dashed green and orange arrows between black points. It shows Project, Intersect and Project operators, an Embedding arrow linking the blue anchor nodes, and a boxed 'Similarity Search' callout pointing to a circled final point. The eye goes first to the colored panels and the large query text.
caption: Task Illustration. Query embedding methods aim to answer multihop logical queries (A) by avoiding explicit knowledge graph traversal and executing the query directly in the embedding space by following the query computation plan (B). Operators are executed in the embedding space (C).
abstract: Neural Graph Databases (NGDBs) facilitate complex logical reasoning over incomplete knowledge structures, yet their training efficiency and expressivity are constrained by rigid query-level batching and structure-exclusive embeddings. We present NGDB-Zoo, a unified framework that resolves these bottlenecks by synergizing operator-level training with semantic augmentation. By decoupling logical operators from query topologies, NGDB-Zoo transforms the training loop into a dynamically scheduled data-flow execution, enabling multi-stream parallelism and achieving a $1.8\times$ - $6.8\times$ throughput compared to baselines. Furthermore, we formalize a decoupled architecture to integrate high-dimensional semantic priors from Pre-trained Text Encoders (PTEs) without triggering I/O stalls or memory overflows. Extensive evaluations on six benchmarks, including massive graphs like ogbl-wikikg2 and ATLAS-Wiki, demonstrate that NGDB-Zoo maintains high GPU utilization across diverse logical patterns and significantly mitigates representation friction in hybrid neuro-symbolic reasoning.
